content.title: Former Virginia Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax fatally shot wife, himself: Police
content.text: Updated: Apr 16, 2026 / 11:37 AM CDT Editor’s Note: This story contains discussions of domestic violence. Reader discretion is advised. If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence or abuse, you can find resources and discreet ways to get help on the National Domestic Violence Hotline website or by calling 1-800-799-7233. (NewsNation) — Former Virginia Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax shot and killed his wife and himself in an apparent murder-suicide, according to local authorities. Fairfax County Police Chief Kevin Davis said the couple were found dead at their home in Annandale, Virginia, on Thursday and pointed to “an ongoing domestic dispute” around a divorce. “I don’t think it’s a secret there’s been divorce proceedings that have been ongoing,” Davis said during a news conference. “Former Lt. Gov. Fairfax was recently served some paperwork associated with an upcoming court proceeding. That apparently led to this incident last night.” 2 teens home during Justin Fairfax shooting, police say Davis said the couple’s two teenage children were at the home when Fairfax shot his wife, Cerina, “several times” before running to a different part of the house and turning the gun on himself. The shooting took place shortly after midnight, and police said one son called 911. Both Fairfax and his wife were pronounced dead at the scene. “Tragic for the children to lose both parents. Extra tragic for them to actually be in the home when it occurred,” Davis said. Police responded to previous call from Fairfax home Davis said authorities responded to a call from the home in January, during which Fairfax, 47, claimed his wife had assaulted him. He said at the time, the couple were separated and living together. During divorce proceedings, Davis said Fairfax’s wife had set up multiple cameras in the home, which allowed police to confirm the allegations were unfounded. Fairfax was not charged with filing a false report. Justin Fairfax’s time in office A Democrat, Fairfax served as lieutenant to Gov. Ralph Northam from 2018 to 2022. Fairfax was the second African American elected statewide in Virginia when the pair won the gubernatorial race in 2017. In 2019, Northam faced calls to resign over a racist photo under his name in a medical school yearbook, which pictured one person in blackface and another dressed in Ku Klux Klan attire. Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax, gestures during the last primary debate in Newport News, Va., Tuesday, June 1, 2021. The primary is held on June 8. (AP Photo/Steve Helber)Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax, gestures during the last primary debate in Newport News, Va., Tuesday, June 1, 2021. The primary is held on June 8. (AP Photo/Steve Helber) Northam later issued a public apology, while denying being either of the individuals in the photograph. In a statement, Fairfax addressed the photo, noting he was “shocked and saddened by the images.” “As someone whose great-great-great-grandfather was enslaved in Virginia, this episode strikes particularly close to home,” Fairfax wrote. “The Governor needed to apologize, and I am glad that he did so. He also reached out to me personally to express his sincere regrets and to apologize.” Justin Fairfax accused of sexual assault In February 2019, Fairfax was accused of sexual assault by two women. The first alleged he assaulted her in a Boston hotel room in 2004, during the Democratic National Convention. The second alleged he assaulted her while they were both students at Duke University in 2000. Fairfax denied the allegations and filed a $400 million lawsuit against CBS, claiming the network defamed him by airing interviews with the two women. A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit in February 2020, after Fairfax failed to prove “actual malice.” Fairfax finished his term before running unsuccessfully for governor in 2021.
